newsitem.title: USA: Amoco, Shell, Sonat units to build natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Shell, Sonat units to build natgas pipeline.

text.p: Affiliates of Amoco Corp, Shell Oil Co and Sonat Inc Monday said they will jointly build and operate a $390 million natural gas pipeline and gas processing system to serve the eastern Gulf of Mexico production region.
Each firm will have a one-third interest in the pipeline project, and Shell and Amoco will jointly own a new gas processing plant to be built in conjunction with the pipeline.
The 210-mile, 36-inch diameter pipeline will have a capacity of 1 billion cubic feet (bcf) per day of natural gas.

It will originate at a new pipeline hub platform to be installed at Main Pass Block 260 and extend 76 miles northward to landfall at Pascagoula, Miss., where the new gas processing plant will be built.
The pipeline will then extend 134 miles further north to interconnect in Mississippi with five interstate pipelines.
Shell and Amoco, major leaseholders in the pipeline's service area, will provide the necessary gas production commitments, in addition to participating in the ownership of the pipeline, they said.

Construction is scheduled to begin in late 1997, and the system is expected to begin service in mid 1998. When the system is completed, Sonat will operate the pipeline and Amoco will operate the gas plant.
Shell Oil Co is the U.S.-based subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch oil company Royal Dutch/Shell.
